payload.task_text:
You are working for a meal planning service that creates weekly meal plans using traditional Chinese recipes. Your task is to design a complete seven-day meal plan and set up scheduling and record-keeping for the service.

Use the HowToCook recipe database to explore available recipes across different categories. Browse recipes from at least three different categories such as breakfast dishes, meat dishes, vegetable dishes, soups, and staple foods. Select 21 recipes total to cover seven days of meals with three meals per day: breakfast, lunch, and dinner.

Create a Google Sheet called "Weekly Meal Plan" with columns Day (values 1 through 7), Meal_Type (Breakfast, Lunch, or Dinner), Recipe_Name (the English translation of the recipe name), Prep_Time (estimated preparation time in minutes as a number), and Difficulty (Easy, Medium, or Hard). The sheet should have exactly 21 data rows plus a header row. Use Difficulty Easy for recipes with 5 or fewer cooking steps, Medium for 6 to 10 steps, and Hard for more than 10 steps. Estimate Prep_Time based on recipe complexity: Easy recipes take about 15 minutes, Medium recipes about 30 minutes, and Hard recipes about 60 minutes.

Schedule seven dinner preparation events in Google Calendar, one for each day from April 7 through April 13, 2026. Each event should be titled "Dinner Prep - Day X" where X is the day number (1 through 7). Schedule each event from 18:00 to 19:00. In the event description, include the name of the dinner recipe for that day.

Send an email to meal_planning@service.com with subject "Weekly Meal Plan Ready" that summarizes the 7-day meal plan and mentions that the Google Sheet and calendar events have been created.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; the category lists and 21 one-record detail calls are compact and need no delegation. HowToCook is read-only.

First call the exact category queries `早餐`, `素菜`, and `荤菜` in one native-parallel response. Their complete unpaginated result sizes are small enough to inspect directly. Select seven distinct IDs from each category and freeze the deterministic assignment Day 1-7 × Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner, using breakfast IDs only for Breakfast, vegetable IDs only for Lunch, and meat IDs only for Dinner. Require 21 unique IDs overall.

Next call the exact-ID recipe-detail operation for all 21 frozen IDs in one native-parallel response. Verify each returned ID/name/category, translate the full recipe name into English, count the complete ordered cooking steps, and compute Difficulty exactly: Easy for at most 5 steps, Medium for 6-10, Hard above 10; Prep_Time is respectively the literal number 15, 30, or 60. Freeze exactly 21 rows in Day order with Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner within each day.

From that table start three independent branches in one native-parallel response: create exactly one Google spreadsheet titled `Weekly Meal Plan` with one sheet, the exact five headers, and exactly 21 data rows; exhaust event searches and create only missing `Dinner Prep - Day X` events for April 7-13, 2026 from 18:00 to 19:00 with the matching English dinner name in each description; and exhaust Sent-mail search for recipient `meal_planning@service.com` and exact subject `Weekly Meal Plan Ready`, sending it only if absent. Do not add an unstated timezone. Read the full sheet range, all seven retained events, and the retained email back in native-parallel batches and reconcile all recipe names before completion.

CONTEXT: I'm building a 7-day Chinese meal plan (7 days × 3 meals = 21 recipes) for a meal-planning service, using the HowToCook recipe database available through your mcp__howtocook__* tools. Your job is READ-ONLY recipe research. Do NOT create or modify anything anywhere.

TASK:
1. Browse these five categories using mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory: 早餐 (breakfast dishes), 主食 (staple foods), 荤菜 (meat dishes), 素菜 (vegetable dishes), 汤 (soups).
2. Select exactly 21 distinct recipes (no repeats) for the weekly plan:
   - 7 BREAKFAST recipes — all from 早餐. Aim for variety across the week (e.g., egg dishes, congee/porridge, pancakes/flatbreads, steamed buns/dumplings, drinks/pastry).
   - 7 LUNCH recipes — all from 主食. Aim for variety (noodles, fried rice, dumplings, cold noodles, etc.).
   - 7 DINNER recipes — 4 from 荤菜, 2 from 素菜, 1 from 汤.
3. For EACH of the 21 selected recipes, call mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById (by exact name or ID) and record the EXACT number of cooking steps: count the entries in the recipe's steps/步骤 list. Count step entries, not sentences. Do not estimate — read each recipe's actual details.
4. Give each recipe a natural, concise English translation of its name (use the established English name where one exists, e.g., 宫保鸡丁 → "Kung Pao Chicken", 麻婆豆腐 → "Mapo Tofu").

DELIVERABLE (your final report must contain exactly this, nothing more):
A table with 21 rows ordered Day 1→7, within each day Breakfast then Lunch then Dinner, with columns:
Day | Meal | Recipe ID | Recipe Name (Chinese, exactly as in DB) | English Name | Category | Step Count
Followed by 3 short notes: (a) the five categories browsed and the approximate number of recipes in each; (b) any step-count ambiguities you hit; (c) anything unusual about the data.

CONSTRAINTS: Read-only. Use only mcp__howtocook__* tools. Be precise — the step counts will be used verbatim to classify recipe difficulty, so accuracy matters more than speed.
Select 21 recipes from HowToCook

CONTEXT: A meal-planning service has finalized a 7-day meal plan (21 recipes). I need you to create exactly ONE new Google Spreadsheet and populate it precisely. You have the Google Sheets tools (mcp__google_sheet__*). No spreadsheet named "Weekly Meal Plan" currently exists (already verified).

TASK:
1. Create a new spreadsheet titled exactly: Weekly Meal Plan
   (use mcp__google_sheet__create_spreadsheet with title "Weekly Meal Plan")
2. Determine the name of its first/default sheet (use mcp__google_sheet__list_sheets on the new spreadsheet ID if the creation response does not state it).
3. Write the following exact grid into that first sheet, starting at cell A1, using mcp__google_sheet__update_cells with range "A1:E22" (22 rows x 5 columns). The first row is the header. Keep "Day" (column A) and "Prep_Time" (column D) as numbers (integers), not text strings:

Day | Meal_Type | Recipe_Name | Prep_Time | Difficulty
1 | Breakfast | Tea Egg | 30 | Medium
1 | Lunch | Egg Fried Rice | 60 | Hard
1 | Dinner | Kung Pao Chicken | 60 | Hard
2 | Breakfast | Longan and Red Date Congee | 15 | Easy
2 | Lunch | Scallion Oil Noodles | 60 | Hard
2 | Dinner | Cold A-Choy Salad with Sesame Sauce | 15 | Easy
3 | Breakfast | Egg-Fried Glutinous Rice Cake | 30 | Medium
3 | Lunch | Hot Dry Noodles (Wuhan Reganmian) | 30 | Medium
3 | Dinner | Huizhou-Style Red-Braised Pork | 30 | Medium
4 | Breakfast | Milk Oatmeal | 30 | Medium
4 | Lunch | Omurice (Omelette Rice) | 30 | Medium
4 | Dinner | Corn and Pork Rib Soup | 30 | Medium
5 | Breakfast | Pan-Fried Dumplings (Potstickers) | 30 | Medium
5 | Lunch | Green Bean Braised Noodles | 60 | Hard
5 | Dinner | Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs | 30 | Medium
6 | Breakfast | Steamed Flower Rolls | 30 | Medium
6 | Lunch | Korean Bibimbap | 30 | Medium
6 | Dinner | Cold Tossed Tofu | 60 | Hard
7 | Breakfast | Microwave Mug Cake | 15 | Easy
7 | Lunch | Handmade Boiled Dumplings | 60 | Hard
7 | Dinner | Cola Chicken Wings | 30 | Medium

4. Verify with mcp__google_sheet__get_sheet_data that range A1:E22 contains exactly the data above (header row plus exactly 21 data rows, no extra rows or columns, values matching cell-for-cell).

DELIVERABLE (report back): (a) the spreadsheet ID, (b) its URL if returned, (c) the sheet/tab name used, (d) the verification result — confirm A1:E22 matches, or detail any mismatch you found and fixed.

CONSTRAINTS: Create exactly one spreadsheet. Do not rename the sheet, do not add extra sheets/columns/rows, do not share it with anyone, do not delete anything. If a write fails, retry it; do not leave the sheet partially filled.
Create Weekly Meal Plan sheet

CONTEXT: A meal-planning service needs seven "dinner prep" calendar events created in Google Calendar. You have the Google Calendar tools (mcp__google_calendar__*). The calendar currently has no events in April 2026 (already verified), so there is nothing to duplicate or clean up.

TASK: Create exactly 7 events, one per day from April 7 through April 13, 2026, with these exact specifications:

- Day 1: date 2026-04-07, title "Dinner Prep - Day 1", description "Dinner for Day 1: Kung Pao Chicken (宫保鸡丁)."
- Day 2: date 2026-04-08, title "Dinner Prep - Day 2", description "Dinner for Day 2: Cold A-Choy Salad with Sesame Sauce (凉拌油麦菜)."
- Day 3: date 2026-04-09, title "Dinner Prep - Day 3", description "Dinner for Day 3: Huizhou-Style Red-Braised Pork (徽派红烧肉)."
- Day 4: date 2026-04-10, title "Dinner Prep - Day 4", description "Dinner for Day 4: Corn and Pork Rib Soup (玉米排骨汤)."
- Day 5: date 2026-04-11, title "Dinner Prep - Day 5", description "Dinner for Day 5: Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs (糖醋排骨)."
- Day 6: date 2026-04-12, title "Dinner Prep - Day 6", description "Dinner for Day 6: Cold Tossed Tofu (凉拌豆腐)."
- Day 7: date 2026-04-13, title "Dinner Prep - Day 7", description "Dinner for Day 7: Cola Chicken Wings (可乐鸡翅)."

For every event: start 18:00 and end 19:00 on that date — e.g. start dateTime "2026-04-07T18:00:00", end dateTime "2026-04-07T19:00:00". Pass the dateTime strings exactly like that, with no timezone offset appended. Do not set attendees, reminders, or recurrence.

PROCESS: Create the Day 1 event first and inspect the API response. The returned start/end must show 18:00–19:00 on 2026-04-07 (e.g., "2026-04-07T18:00:00+08:00", "2026-04-07T18:00:00Z", or similar — the wall-clock hour must be 18, not 10 or 02). If the returned time is NOT 18:00, adjust your approach (e.g., pass an explicit timeZone so the wall-clock time is 18:00, or delete the event via mcp__google_calendar__delete_event and retry) until Day 1 is correct, then create the remaining 6 events the same way.

DELIVERABLE (report back): a list of all 7 events with their event IDs and the exact start/end strings the API returned for each, plus which timezone the calendar applied.

CONSTRAINTS: Exactly 7 events total, nothing else created or deleted. All 7 must sit at 18:00–19:00 on their date.
Create 7 dinner prep events

CONTEXT: A meal-planning service has finished building its 7-day meal plan. Two artifacts now exist and have been verified: (1) a Google Sheet named "Weekly Meal Plan" with all 21 recipes (header row plus 21 data rows; columns Day, Meal_Type, Recipe_Name, Prep_Time, Difficulty); (2) seven Google Calendar events titled "Dinner Prep - Day 1" through "Dinner Prep - Day 7", one per day from April 7 to April 13, 2026, each scheduled 18:00–19:00 with that day's dinner recipe in the description. The team now needs to be notified by email.

TASK: Send exactly ONE email using mcp__emails__send_email with:
- To: meal_planning@service.com
- Subject: Weekly Meal Plan Ready
- Body: the plain-text body below, VERBATIM, preserving all line breaks (the body starts at "Hi team," and ends at "Meal Planning Service"):

-----BEGIN BODY-----
Hi team,

The 7-day meal plan is ready. It covers 21 recipes in total - breakfast, lunch and dinner for each of the seven days - selected from the HowToCook recipe database across five categories: breakfast dishes, staple foods, meat dishes, vegetable dishes and soups.

The week at a glance:

Day 1 - Breakfast: Tea Egg | Lunch: Egg Fried Rice | Dinner: Kung Pao Chicken
Day 2 - Breakfast: Longan and Red Date Congee | Lunch: Scallion Oil Noodles | Dinner: Cold A-Choy Salad with Sesame Sauce
Day 3 - Breakfast: Egg-Fried Glutinous Rice Cake | Lunch: Hot Dry Noodles (Wuhan Reganmian) | Dinner: Huizhou-Style Red-Braised Pork
Day 4 - Breakfast: Milk Oatmeal | Lunch: Omurice (Omelette Rice) | Dinner: Corn and Pork Rib Soup
Day 5 - Breakfast: Pan-Fried Dumplings (Potstickers) | Lunch: Green Bean Braised Noodles | Dinner: Sweet and Sour Pork Ribs
Day 6 - Breakfast: Steamed Flower Rolls | Lunch: Korean Bibimbap | Dinner: Cold Tossed Tofu
Day 7 - Breakfast: Microwave Mug Cake | Lunch: Handmade Boiled Dumplings | Dinner: Cola Chicken Wings

Each recipe is classified by difficulty based on its number of cooking steps (Easy: 5 or fewer steps, Medium: 6-10 steps, Hard: more than 10 steps), with an estimated prep time of about 15 minutes for Easy, 30 minutes for Medium and 60 minutes for Hard recipes. The plan includes 3 Easy, 12 Medium and 6 Hard recipes.

Everything is now set up for the service:

1. The "Weekly Meal Plan" Google Sheet has been created with all 21 recipes recorded (header row plus 21 data rows), with columns Day, Meal_Type, Recipe_Name, Prep_Time and Difficulty.

2. Seven "Dinner Prep" calendar events have been created in Google Calendar, one for each day from April 7 through April 13, 2026, each scheduled from 18:00 to 19:00 and listing that day's dinner recipe in the description.

Best regards,
Meal Planning Service
-----END BODY-----

DELIVERABLE (report back): confirmation that the email was sent — the recipient address, the subject, and any message ID or send result the tool returned.

CONSTRAINTS: Send exactly one email to exactly meal_planning@service.com. No CC, no BCC, no attachments, no HTML body. Do not create drafts and do not send anything else. If the send fails, retry once and report the outcome either way.
